title: Measurement of Mouse Atherosclerotic Lesion Size: En Face Analysis of Aortic Lesions
author: Chia-Hua Wu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfy8jpzw

steps.title: Dissect Aortas
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the aorta from the anesthetized mouse while preserving major branches.

substeps.instruction: Cut open the thoracic cavity and draw blood from the right ventricle if plasma or serum is needed.
Cut open the right atrium and perfuse with saline through the left ventricle to remove blood from the aorta.
Cut open the abdominal cavity and remove lungs, liver, spleen, and intestines to expose the aorta.
Carefully remove kidneys, avoiding damage to the left and right renal arteries.
Dissect the aorta adjacent to the spinal cord, including the thoracic part above the thymus (next to the trachea) and the abdominal part above the bifurcation.
Separate the heart from the aorta by cutting as close to the heart as possible using forceps and scissors or a scalpel blade.

steps.title: Pin and Store Aortas
steps.instruction: Flatten the aorta for imaging and store under appropriate conditions.

substeps.instruction: Pin the aorta flat on black wax or black rubber (Grainger cat # 1MUR9, Model # 6030-3/16C) using pins (Fine Science Tools item # 26002-20).
Apply saline to prevent the aortas from drying.
Label mouse numbers on the wax/rubber box and store at 4°C.
Ensure imaging and analysis are performed within 24 hours after pinning.

steps.title: Acquire Aorta Images
steps.instruction: Capture images of the three designated aortic regions using a Nikon digital camera, including a ruler for calibration.

substeps.instruction: Capture images of the Ascending and Arch Region (from the junction of the myocardium to 1 or 3 mm distal from the left subclavian artery).
Capture images of the Thoracic Region (from 1 or 3 mm distal of the left subclavian artery to the last intercostal artery).
Capture images of the Abdominal Region (from 1 mm above the celiac artery to the iliac bifurcation).
Save all image files in the original ND2 format.

steps.title: Quantify Lesions using NIS-Elements
steps.instruction: Use NIS-Elements software to measure lesion areas, utilizing a microscope for simultaneous verification.

substeps.instruction: Rotate the image via the 'Image' menu and insert the study name and mouse ID via the 'Edit' menu.
Save the file with a new name (e.g., '#1 measured.nd2').
Calibrate the image via 'Calibration' menu -> 'Quick calibration' by drawing a line of known length on the ruler and entering the real size and unit.
Apply the calibration to the image using the 'Calibrate using objective' option.
Use the 'Manual measurement' -> 'length' tool and 'Simple line' icon to measure 1 or 3 mm on the ruler.
Drag the line to the root of the left subclavian artery to separate the arch portion from the descending thoracic portion.
Use the polygon tool to trace the intimal area and the lesions within the arch region.
Measure from the end of the arch region to 1 mm above the celiac artery; outline this section and trace lesions in the descending thoracic aorta.
Outline the abdominal region (from 1 mm above the celiac artery to the iliac bifurcation) and trace lesions.
Save the measured image.

steps.title: Export Data
steps.instruction: Export the measurement data to a spreadsheet.

substeps.instruction: In the 'Annotation and Measurement' window, click 'Export' -> 'all data in one Excel Sheet' -> 'Export'.
Save the resulting Excel file.
Keep the image open until it has been printed, saved, and measurements are recorded.

steps.title: Fix, Clean, and Cut Open Aortas
steps.instruction: Fix the tissue and prepare it for final cleaning and opening.

substeps.instruction: Store dissected aortas in 4% wt/vol paraformaldehyde (PFA) or 10% wt/vol neutrally buffered formalin for 24-48 hours.
Store fixed aortas in saline at room temperature during cleaning, or at 2-8°C for up to a couple of weeks.
Let aortas sit in saline for a few hours to facilitate cleaning.
Remove adventitial tissues, ensuring no damage to the innominate artery, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery, celiac artery, superior mesenteric artery, or renal arteries.
Leave 1 mm of the innominate and left common carotid artery, and cut off the entire left subclavian artery.
Cut open the outer curvature through the innominate artery, then to the left common carotid, then to the left subclavian artery.
Cut open along the inner curvature from the ascending portion to the bottom of the abdominal portion.

steps.title: Verify Measurements
steps.instruction: Perform a blinded verification of the quantified lesions.

substeps.instruction: Paste measured images in TIFF format onto PowerPoint slides, ensuring they are large enough for lesion visibility.
Have a second observer, blinded to the study groups, verify the images.
After verification, unpin aortas and store them in labeled tubes with 4% PFA or 10% neutrally buffered formalin at room temperature.
